OptogeneticsConfig.description:
Zapit optogenetic stimulation: av-dome's fields, plus lead_time.

The stimulation sites, laser power and ramp-down are set in the Zapit stimulus config loaded in Zapit, not
here. Bonsai reads the same file to list its conditions (stimLocations01, stimLocations02, ...). Every trial of
an optogenetics experiment sends Zapit a condition: laser-on trials with the laser on, all others as sham trials
with the laser off, so galvo noise and masking light are the same on every trial. The stimulus is continuous: it
starts at the trial's start (beep 0: the trigger pulse on a hardware-triggered rig), lead_time before the first
tone pip, and Bonsai stops it at the trial's outcome, or after stim_duration if that comes first. Zapit's host,
port and triggering are rig.yml's zapit block.

zapitConfigPath.description: Path to the Zapit stimulus config loaded in Zapit. Its top-level stimLocations01, stimLocations02, ... entries are the conditions: numbered 1 to N with no gaps, each with an offRampDownDuration_ms of at least 100 ms
zapitConfigPath.title: ZapitConfigPath

stimProbability.description: Probability that a trial after the warmup is a laser-on trial, shared equally by every condition in the Zapit stimulus config, a laser-on control site included. All other trials are sham trials: Zapit is sent a condition with the laser off
stimProbability.title: StimProbability

stimDelay.description: av-dome's field, kept at 0: Zapit ignores a start delay for the continuous stimulus this task uses. The laser starts at the trial's start, lead_time before the first tone pip
stimDelay.title: StimDelay

stimDuration.description: Longest the stimulus runs in one trial, in seconds from onset, timed by Bonsai; the laser then ramps down over the condition's offRampDownDuration_ms. A safety cap: the stimulus normally stops at the trial's outcome. With optogenetics on it must be at least trialStructure.closedLoopDuration (the time limit, 12 s) + lead_time + 0.25 s, so it never ends a timed-out trial's laser early; on a stage without timeLimit a longer trial loses its stimulus
stimDuration.title: StimDuration

leadTime.description: How long the stimulus runs before the first tone pip, in seconds: a multiple of the 50 ms beep, from 0.05 to 0.2. The first pip moves to beep lead_time / 50 ms on every trial of an optogenetics experiment, laser-on or sham, so trial timing does not reveal laser-on trials. At most 0.2 s: licks before the first pip count toward the wrong-lick limits, and a longer lead could end a trial before its first pip
leadTime.title: LeadTime

excludeRepeats.description: Whether repeat trials are excluded from stimulation (av-dome's; this task has no repeat trials)
excludeRepeats.title: ExcludeRepeats

pseudorandomSelection.description: Draw conditions from shuffled queues, one for laser-on and one for sham trials, so each condition is used equally often, rather than independently each trial
pseudorandomSelection.title: PseudorandomSelection

warmupTrials.description: Trials at the experiment's start that are all sham trials, with the laser off
warmupTrials.title: WarmupTrials

Truncation.description:
Where the cue switches off on a truncated trial (a stage's truncationFraction says how many).

On a truncated trial the cue (tone and grating) switches off part way along the sweep. Everything else about
the trial is unchanged, so it is still rewarded as normal: the animal has to keep going and find the reward
zone without the cue.

points.description: Where the cue switches off, as a fraction of the sweep on a log scale, split evenly over truncated trials. The reward floor is at about 0.8
points.title: Points
